grammar_concept.title: There is / There are
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'there is' with a singular or uncountable noun, and 'there are' with a plural noun, to say that something exists or is present.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: "There is/are" says what exists in a place — a room, a bag, a city. The verb changes depending on whether you are talking about one thing or many things.
grammar_concept.example: There is one chair. There are three books on the table.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Há uma cadeira. Há três livros na mesa.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português, "há" nunca muda de forma, quer se fale de uma coisa ou de muitas ("há um livro" / "há três livros") — isso leva a usar sempre "there is", mesmo com plural, dizendo "there is three books" em vez de "there are three books".
grammar_concept.correction: Use "there are" sempre que o substantivo a seguir estiver no plural — mesmo que em português a palavra "há" nunca mude de forma.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Describing a room: "There are four chairs and there is one table."

vocabulary.definition_en: used to ask about the number of countable things
example_sentences: How many books are there on the table?

vocabulary.definition_en: used after a number to say the exact hour
the first day of the working week
example_sentences: I have my English class on Monday.

exercises.prompt: Complete: ___ one apple on the table.
exercises.explanation: "Apple" está no singular, por isso usa-se "there is".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Alguns alunos tentam usar "is there" (forma de pergunta) numa frase afirmativa.

exercises.prompt: Complete: ___ five students in the class.
exercises.explanation: "Students" está no plural, por isso usa-se "there are".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Erro comum: usar "there is" com um substantivo no plural, por transferência do português "há", que nunca muda de forma.

exercises.prompt: What do you say to ask about the number of things?
exercises.explanation: "How many" é usado com substantivos contáveis (books, students); "how much" é usado com incontáveis (water, money).
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Confundir "how many" com "how much" é muito comum entre iniciantes.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. How many chairs are there in the room?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "There are four chairs and one table in the room."
exercises.transcript: There are four chairs and one table in the room.

exercises.prompt: Read: "My English class is on Monday and Wednesday, at seven o'clock." What time is the class?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente "at seven o'clock".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Há três cadeiras e uma mesa na sala."
correct_answer: There are three chairs and one table in the room.
There are three chairs and a table in the room.
exercises.explanation: "Cadeiras" está no plural, por isso pede "there are"; "mesa" está no singular ("one table"/"a table") mas junta-se à mesma frase com "and".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "there is" para a frase inteira, ignorando que "cadeiras" está no plural, é o erro mais comum aqui.

steps.content: Practise linking numbers to "o'clock" smoothly: "three o'clock" /θriː əˈklɒk/ is said as one flowing phrase, not two separate words with a pause.

steps.prompt: Describe your room: say how many chairs, tables and windows there are, using "there is/are".
Write 3 sentences about your weekly schedule: what day and what time your English class (or work) is.
